title: SDK Ecosystem Playbooks & Activation Pipeline
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Objective: Create a repeatable, measurable playbook and execution pipeline to increase developer activation and first-success for Redwood SDKs (Node, Python, Go) and quickstarts. This ticket coordinates PM, Docs, DX engineering, and Design to produce: 1) canonical quickstart templates (starter app + one-line SDK integration), 2) SDK usage playbooks for common workloads (chat, embeddings, streaming), 3) activation tracking pipeline for OKRs (instrumentation + dashboards), and 4) rollout checklist and fallback mitigation.
success_criteria: 1) 30% lift in 7-day activation rate for new signups that use SDK quickstarts (baseline measured in dashboard). 2) Time-to-first-success (meaningful API call + example run) under 10 minutes on average for 90% of users following the quickstart. 3) Updated SDK docs and 3 language quickstarts published with tests and CI. 4) Activation metrics surfaced in growth & product dashboards (at least 4 visualizations).
deliverables: Canonical quickstart repo with CI, tests, and templates for Node/Python/Go
SDK playbook docs: integration patterns, recommended batching/timeout defaults, error-handling examples
Instrumentation plan: events, schemas, and dashboard wireframes
Rollout checklist: staged release, telemetry validation, rollback criteria
notes: Trade-offs considered: - Deep example apps vs minimal onboarding friction: decided on minimal starter + one advanced reference app. - Strict SDK defaults (opinionated) vs flexible options: opt for safe defaults with simple override pattern. - Full telemetry with PII concerns: capture only non-identifying activation events; link to legal for approval.
